referees.quote: the key findings of this manuscript seem incremental... Unless the authors can provide and explain experimental discovery that distinguishes (SnS)1.15(TaS2)... I cannot recommend this paper for publication in Nature Communications.
I also think the provided theoretical explanation is not the only possible one, and the paper has other drawbacks, so I am not very convinced that the current version belongs to Nat. Comm.
I am unable to recommend the manuscript for publication in Nature Communications at this stage. However, it may become suitable once the authors have carefully addressed the points detailed below.
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

note: The file starts at Version 0 with no sign of a transfer from another journal, so the first round is Version 0. R1 is borderline: its rejection is conditional ('Unless the authors can...'), but it rests on the work being incremental, so it maps to 'reject'. R2's 'not very convinced that the current version belongs' together with its substantive requests maps to 'major revision'. R4 is an early-career co-reviewer and did not say which report they co-signed. Their recommendation is assigned as R3's ('major revision') on weak evidence: in later rounds the R3 slot also carries the co-review statement. Treat R4's recommendation as uncertain; it could instead match R1 ('reject') or R2 ('major revision').
